cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Believe This with Me
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into treating your impossible explanation as the most useful version of events.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. The office kettle's on strike. Help me negotiate before the clients arrive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've filled it twice. It still won't boil.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then water isn't its grievance. Tell it we'll stop leaving it alone after meetings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can take it into the meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Give it my chair. A seat at the table should get us tea.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs negotiation, A3 assigns a promise to the kettle, and A5 grants A's chair as the authorized concession that should end the strike.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 filling failure rules out water in A3; B4 inclusion offer becomes A5 a seat at the table.

relationship.evidence: B2 has tried a real fix and B4 offers practical participation instead of continued skepticism.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns B4 helpful solution into the next literal bargaining term.

specificity.evidence: A1 office kettle and arriving clients establish why tea is needed now.
